_comment: RED baseline (RLOO variant), second attempt: identical to red250.json except the advantage rule, which is R4. red250.json is kept unchanged as the record of what produced runs/red250. R4 is A_{i,t} = A_seq_i + red_alpha * (r^final_{i,t} - mean_t r^final_{i,t}), with A_seq_i RLOO's own leave-one-out advantage -- the sequence contrast carries the level and RED's redistribution only decides which tokens within a response receive it. R3, the first rule, subtracted the sequence-scale baseline b_i off every token instead; on a group whose rewards are all negative that made every token's advantage positive, the update stopped being contrastive, and runs/red250 collapsed to degenerate 2-token responses from rollout 50 and then crashed at 68. See red/RED_REPRO_NOTES.md 2.2 for the measurements and the retirement. Everything else is still copied from formal250.json so this arm stays comparable with GRPO, VPO-RM and P2T; only the credit assignment differs. Paper-specific notes: (1) beta_c is RED Eq. (7)'s convex-combination weight, 1.0 removes the sparse sequence term entirely; (2) the KL coefficient rides in 'beta' and is applied INSIDE the reward per Eq. (8), so the trainer applies no separate KL loss term; (3) clip_eps and advantage_std_floor_fraction are carried for config parity. advantage_std_floor_fraction is genuinely unread by a RED update (RED does not standardise the advantage), but clip_eps IS read in three places that do not clip the objective: the validation below, the rollout_direct_ratio_clip_fraction metric, and the startup gate on trainer-vs-sampler agreement. Do not set it to 0 or 1 to mean 'no clipping' -- that fails validation. The run manifest stamps red_clipping, red_advantage_rule and red_alpha so the actual behaviour is never ambiguous after the fact. TABLE 7 DEVIATIONS are kept deliberately, not overlooked: beta is 0.03 against the paper's 0.02, group_size is 8 against RLOO sample K 4, max_response_tokens is 2048 against 1024/688/512, and the harmfulness/helpfulness two-model setup of the paper's SafeRLHF experiments is not implemented. Aligning any of those would break comparability with this project's other arms, so they stay recorded as deviations in RED_REPRO_NOTES.md section 1. DEVICE PLAN: four cards, actor and reward plus a tensor-parallel pair. Launch with RED_GPUS=0,1,2,3 so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is set to exactly 0,1,2,3: the trainer's device-plan check requires the visible list to equal range(2 + vllm_tensor_parallel_size), i.e. [0,1,2,3] here, so this configuration runs WITH the check active rather than in the unset-CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES mode that skips it. red250 ran in that skipped mode with tp=1 on three cards; this run uses tp=2 across 2 and 3, which is the same generation layout p2t250 used, so the two arms' generation is configured alike. The consequence to keep in mind is that tensor parallelism can differ from tp=1 in the last bits of the sampler log-probs, so this run is not bit-comparable to red250's generation; it is comparable to p2t250's, which is the comparison the arm exists for. vllm_gpus names PHYSICAL cards handed straight to the subprocess as its own CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, and with tp=2 it takes both entries. push_every is 5: the owner approved autopush, knowing commits land on the local p2t-baseline branch and are pushed to p2t-origin/main, and that autopush stages the whole tree (git add -A). checkpoint_interval and keep_checkpoints stay at the sibling's 20/2 even though red250's two surviving checkpoints were both already past its collapse and its last healthy state was never recoverable: tests/red/test_trainer.py pins every shared training parameter against formal250.json, and this arm's whole purpose is to differ from its siblings in the credit assignment and nothing else. The protection against a repeat is the health gate instead. Launch the watcher with stop-on-problem so a collapse costs the rollouts it took to detect rather than the whole budget: bash red/scripts/watch_red.sh red250b 30 stop-on-problem. With a 20-rollout checkpoint interval that can still cost up to 20 rollouts of recoverable progress when it fires, which is the accepted trade for not diverging from the sibling's cadence; change both numbers here and in the sibling arm's config together if that trade is ever revisited
